boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Wood Lake record (September 23, 1862) in Operations to Suppress the Sioux Uprising [August-September 1862]. Sibley's march from Fort Ridgely from September 19, the prisoners held by the Dakota and the later surrender at Camp Release are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives volunteer troops of about 1,500 (US bounds 1,500 and 1,500) and the Santee Sioux without figures; the frozen description says Sibley set out with 1,500 and escaped an ambush by 700 warriors. Sibley says the camp was attacked by about 300 Indians, and relays the half-breed Joseph Campbell's statement that 800 were assembled within 2 miles but the greater part took no share in the fight; he names his cavalry as only 27 and says the other companies of the Sixth were held back to defend the camp. Marshall reports five companies of the Seventh engaged.
claims.rationale: Column, attacking and assembled figures of different scopes: the 1,500 is the column leaving Fort Ridgely on September 19; the 300 attackers, the 27 cavalry and Campbell's 800 assembled (relayed hearsay) refer to September 23; the frozen 700 is not traced. No account by the Dakota side was inspected; every statement of their numbers, aims and losses comes from their opponents or from the NPS summary. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel Henry Hastings Sibley and Little Crow (no rank recorded); the live page gives Sibley as brigadier general and tags Little Crow [CS], neither adopted. Sibley's 1865 note says he was acting as colonel under the Governor's authority and had not yet received the order to report to Pope. Sibley sent Gorman's Renville Rangers to check the attack and ordered Marshall with five companies of the Seventh to the support of the Third; Marshall led the charge. The inspected reports mention Little Crow only in Campbell's relayed statement.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested reports; no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory; NPS says Sibley's force won the day and calls Wood Lake the first decisive defeat of the Sioux. Sibley says the Indians, repulsed at all points after about two hours, retired with precipitation.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads US 37 and Indian losses unknown; the live field reads 66 (US 41; CS 25). Sibley gives 4 killed and 35 to 40 wounded; he relays Campbell's 30 Indians killed and says 14 bodies were found and buried. Marshall gives one killed, two wounded and one bruised in his five companies and 7 enemy dead brought in by his command.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Sibley's 14 buried and Marshall's 7 may overlap.

open_questions: The Dakota side's account, the source of the frozen 700 and 1,500, Sibley's field returns, the later surrender at Camp Release, histories of the war and maps remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Sibley's September 23, 1862 report (with his 1865 note) and Marshall's report of the same day are interested accounts; Marshall's was transmitted with Sibley's, but each is a separate author family. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
